status: source-informed declared accounting policy; not observed 2025 dispatch or loss reconstruction
source_vintage: Primary NYISO manuals retrieved in 2026; their 2025 historical editions were not independently verified.

actual_load_input_lineage.time_label_assumption_retained: P58C labels treated as hour beginnings following prior empirical repository timing audit; not a provider integration specification

direct_source_facts.finding: Real-time actual zonal load is calculated from generation and net interchange using telemetry; its integrated series is a time-weighted hourly value.
direct_source_facts.model_implication: Treat the P58 balance quantity as gross boundary demand before separating modeled internal losses from delivered bus load.
direct_source_facts.qualification: The definition supports this balance interpretation but does not supply 2025 zonal loss values or certify the model's exact physical meter locations.

direct_source_facts.finding: The short-term real-time demand forecast excludes transmission losses; scheduling adds zonal losses calculated by RTC/RTD power flow.
direct_source_facts.model_implication: Do not transfer this forecast convention to the separately defined public actual-load balance series.
direct_source_facts.qualification: A forecast rule alone cannot establish that P58 actual load is delivered bus PD.

direct_source_facts.section: Data Type FLOW; General Instructions / Energy balance
direct_source_facts.finding: Demand plus net exported tie flow balances net generation. Positive reported FLOW means export from the reporting balancing authority.
direct_source_facts.model_implication: Negate NYIS-reported FLOW to obtain positive NY import targets and use a consistent reporting perspective.
direct_source_facts.qualification: Generation and interchange must use compatible reporting boundaries.

direct_source_facts.finding: Reporting generally follows physical tie boundaries rather than ownership or dispatch. Dynamic-transfer exceptions require consistent agreements among affected balancing authorities communicated to EIA.
direct_source_facts.model_implication: Preserve the existing boundary-scope qualification, including NYISO-market resources physically outside NY and unresolved counterpart differences.
direct_source_facts.qualification: Market admission does not by itself prove EIA physical-balancing-area inclusion.

direct_source_facts.section: D and NG; pumped storage and batteries
direct_source_facts.finding: Known grid energy used for storage is normally excluded from demand and included as negative net generation; a separate reporting fallback is defined.
direct_source_facts.model_implication: Do not treat storage or pumped hydro as unconstrained loss-balancing resources without energy and availability evidence.
direct_source_facts.qualification: No storage energy constraint has been reconstructed in this experiment.

interpretation.NY_P58: gross boundary demand: generation plus net import contains demand and losses inside the chosen meter boundary
interpretation.external_PD: frozen delivered-demand proxy; no observed external 2025 regional load is claimed
interpretation.native_PG: the existing 1436-row profile remains fixed, including the native reference generator
interpretation.HQ: the bus48 equivalent remains the fixed signed source-target injection and is excluded from loss balancing

loss_ownership.same_NY_zone_corridor: all real loss belongs to that zone
loss_ownership.different_NY_zones_corridor: half belongs to each original physical terminal zone
loss_ownership.external_internal_corridor: all real loss belongs to its external region
loss_ownership.cross_border_corridor: all real loss belongs to the external area under the NY-terminal receipt convention, including reverse-flow hours
loss_ownership.numeric_section_nodes: sum losses over the original parent corridor; never determine ownership from numerical interior-node tags
loss_ownership.zero_injection_nodes: preserve zero active/reactive demand at added station and numerical section buses
loss_ownership.GS_and_DC_losses: currently required to be exactly zero; a nonzero value requires an explicit ownership extension
loss_ownership.status: declared model accounting; not certified NYISO zonal meter allocation

allocation.NY_delivered_PD: subtract the assigned zonal loss by scaling the existing nonnegative zonal bus-load shares
allocation.NY_QD: scale by the same factor, preserving the existing assumed power factor; QD is not observed telemetry
allocation.external_PG: baseline_PG plus regional assigned loss allocated by frozen within-region generation shares, with bounded redistribution on saturation
allocation.external_limits: restore original finite Pmin/Pmax; retain fixed apparent-power capability proxy and recompute Q circle allowance at revised PG
allocation.infeasibility: reject exhausted external headroom or nonpositive zonal delivered demand; do not enlarge limits or clip unaccounted loss
allocation.reference: a numerical angle reference may absorb temporary iteration residuals; final native-reference PG must return to its input within tolerance

boundary_contract.regional_net: preserve actual NYIS-reported EIA930 net-import targets at NY physical corridor terminals
boundary_contract.controlled_transfers: preserve all six signed DC/PAR targets exactly; the AC/DC split retains its original source qualification
boundary_contract.graph_prerequisite: each external region connects to NY and has no active ties to another external region
boundary_contract.internal_interfaces: the seven P32 internal interface series are comparison-only and never fitted by this policy

qualification_gates: AC equations and loss fixed point converge on every reported qualified hour
all native PG and HQ injection retain their source-profile values within reported numerical tolerance
all three modeled regional NY-terminal imports and all six controlled transfers match their targets
the loss ledger counts each active parent-corridor loss exactly once and global power balance closes
all NY delivered loads remain nonnegative and loss fractions are published by zone
external PG stays within finite original P bounds and fixed S capability is not enlarged
report Q capability, voltage, thermal limits, and reactive-control caveats separately from active-balance correctness
compact-model terminal reconstructions retain the original physical-terminal measurements and injections
limited_sensitivity_contract: Alternative allocation of cross-NY-zone corridor loss may be evaluated as explicitly declared accounting sensitivity.
Treating external frozen PD as gross demand rather than delivered-demand proxy is a different boundary interpretation, not the default.
Native fossil participation requires explicit delivered-P58 reinterpretation and synchronized/availability/AGC qualifications; finite box headroom alone is not evidence of real flexibility.
Do not count the same NY losses in both a P58 delivered-load reduction and an added native generation requirement.
material_limitations: The source definition justifies a boundary-balance interpretation but does not validate modeled loss magnitude or exact meter locations.
The historical AC screen shows large synthetic zone-F losses; evaluate revised loss fractions before claiming physical realism.
Frozen model fleet status, positive modeled generation, and original external capability are proxies, not observed commitment or reserves.
Native NYISO-market inclusion and EIA physical-BA reporting may have unresolved scope differences.
The synthetic external grid and engineering impedance/reactive assumptions remain model limitations.
